description: Oceanography explores the science of the sea: its branches, seawater physics and currents, waves and tsunamis, the seafloor, ocean chemistry and life, a hands-on project, sharing what you learn, and how scientists study the ocean.

versions.label: Checked against official scouting.org excerpts (partial verification)

provenance.notes: Requirement numbering and topics were checked against excerpts of official Scouting America pages (scouting.org) returned by a search index on 2026-10-24. The pages themselves could not be opened from the build environment, so wording was not compared word for word and some sub-items may be summarized from partial excerpts. Summaries are ScoutPath's own words.

references.label: Official merit badge page (scouting.org Merit Badge Hub)

requirements.title: Why study the oceans
requirements.summary: The branches of oceanography and why ocean study matters.

requirements.title: Seawater and currents
requirements.summary: Salinity, temperature and density, and how currents affect weather and climate.

requirements.title: Waves
requirements.summary: Storm surges, tsunamis, tides and tidal bores, and sea, swell and surf.

requirements.title: The seafloor
requirements.summary: Drawing and labeling a cross-section of the ocean floor.

requirements.title: Ocean chemistry
requirements.summary: Salts, gases and nutrients in seawater and what changes its saltiness.

requirements.title: Ocean life
requirements.summary: Benthos, nekton and plankton, and phytoplankton in the food chain.

requirements.title: An ocean project
requirements.summary: One option, such as a plankton net, a reef model, temperature readings or satellite tracking.

requirements.title: Sharing what you learn
requirements.summary: One option: a book report, a visit to a research vessel or marine facility, or a talk to your troop.

requirements.title: Research methods
requirements.summary: Methods marine scientists use to study the ocean.
